0.text: I want to connect to a college wireless network.

1.text: Are you a student at University of Namur ?

2.text: To which wireless network do you want to connect ?

4.text:
Connecting to Eduroam.
Your username is your student e-mail address. Your password is the same one you use to log into your school's platform.

5.text: Don't worry, we'll help you! <contact>Contact us</contact> and give us the code below: we'll see right away where you are.

9.text:
No specific configuration is needed: just select the unamur network from the list of available wireless networks.

Then log in with your eID followed by "@unamur.be" as your username (for example adupont@unamur.be) and your usual eID password.
⚠ Careful, it must be @unamur.be and not @student.unamur.be !

You should now be connected to the "unamur" network.

Then log in with your eID followed by "@unamur.be" as your username (for example adupont@unamur.be) and your usual eID password.

If the system asks you to verify the certificate, choose verify / validate / accept, then click Continue. You should then be connected to the "unamur" network.

11.text:
Connecting to the "unamur" network has been tested on the default desktop environments of Ubuntu LTS 14.04, Ubuntu LTS 16.04, Fedora 25 and Fedora 26.

Select the unamur network from the list of available wireless networks. A window asking for the connection settings will open: choose WPA & WPA2 Enterprise as the wireless security and Tunneled TLS as the EAP method / authentication, with phase 2 authentication (Inner Authentication) set to PAP.

As both the anonymous identity and the username, enter your eID followed by "@unamur.be" (for example jdupond@unamur.be), then your usual password.
⚠ Careful, it must be @unamur.be and not @student.unamur.be !

For the CA certificate, use /etc/ssl/certs/DigiCert_High_Assurance_EV_Root_CA.pem — if it isn't present on your system, download the DigiCert High Assurance EV Root CA certificate.

If the system asks you to verify the certificate, make sure the server name is indeed clearpass.unamur.be before validating.

13.text:
Select the unamur network from the list of available wireless networks, then configure the connection with the following settings.

For security, choose 802.1x EAP with the TTLS method, phase 2 authentication set to PAP, and a minimum TLS version (1.0, 1.1 or 1.2 — do not select TLS 1.3). For the CA certificate, use the system certificates, and enter unamur.be as the domain.

As both identity and anonymous identity, enter your eID followed by "@unamur.be" (for example adupont@unamur.be), then your usual password.
⚠ Careful, it must be @unamur.be and not @student.unamur.be !

If the system asks you to verify the certificate, make sure the server name is indeed clearpass.unamur.be before validating.

14.text:
Your eID is the unique identifier that lets you log in to all of the University of Namur's services (for example adupont for Alain Dupont). If someone already has that identifier, yours will be slightly different.

You can find it on your UNamur account.

15.text: You can connect to the eduroam network, available on most university campuses. Use the e-mail address and password of your own institution (for example firstname.lastname@youruniversity.be) — not your UNamur credentials.

16.text:
Check these few points first, they solve most problems:

1. Your username is your eID followed by @unamur.be (not @student.unamur.be), with no spaces.
2. Your password is correct: check it by logging in to your UNamur account.
3. In your device's wifi settings, "forget" the unamur network, then connect again: old credentials are sometimes kept.
4. Your device's date and time are correct, otherwise the network certificate may be rejected.
